# Bitvavo.Net 0.5.0 full LLM context — copy-paste guide to the Bitvavo REST and WebSocket client: exact API surface, quick starts, errors, rate limits, pitfalls.

> Detailed reference for generating correct C#/.NET code with Bitvavo.Net. Routing tables with HTTP verb, path, auth and weight per method: `docs/ai-api-map.md`. Member lists: `Bitvavo.Net/Interfaces/Clients/**`. Design: `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Facts

- NuGet package `Bitvavo.Net`, version 0.5.0 (pre-1.0: the API can still change between minor versions). Repository https://github.com/xkqg/Bitvavo.Net. MIT.
- Targets net8.0, net9.0, net10.0. Built on CryptoExchange.Net 13.1.0 (structure of Kraken.Net 8.6.0, both load in one process).
- Bitvavo is spot only. No futures, no margin, no testnet: `BitvavoEnvironment.Live` is the only environment (REST `https://api.bitvavo.com`, WebSocket `wss://ws.bitvavo.com/v2/`).
- Coverage matches Bitvavo REST API docs v2.10.0. All REST paths sit under `/v2/`.
- Results: REST `HttpResult<T>`, subscriptions `WebSocketResult<UpdateSubscription>`. Protocol errors are results, not exceptions.

## Golden rules for AI code generation

- REST: `BitvavoRestClient` (`IBitvavoRestClient`). WebSocket: `BitvavoSocketClient` (`IBitvavoSocketClient`). Exchange-agnostic: Shared API (`SpotApi.SharedApi`, `IBitvavoSharedApiClient`).
- Never raw `HttpClient` against Bitvavo, never hand-made HMAC. Signing, timestamp, access window and rate limiting are built in.
- Credentials: `new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret)` (not generic `ApiCredentials`). Public endpoints need none.
- Always branch on `result.Success` before reading `result.Data`.
- Every order operation needs an `operatorId` (`long`). Every `clientOrderId` must be a UUID (`Guid.NewGuid().ToString()`).
- Prices must be a multiple of `BitvavoMarket.TickSize`. `PricePrecision` is null on every live market: never use it.
- Fee rates are fractions (`0.0015` = 0.15 %). The Shared API reports percentages.
- Amounts and prices are `decimal` in C# and JSON strings on the wire. `DateTime` is UTC (unix milliseconds on the wire).
- Public endpoints are never signed and count against the per-IP budget; signed endpoints count against the per-account budget.
- Prefer dependency injection for long-running services. With `new`, keep one client and dispose it at shutdown. Do not create a client per request.
- Store subscriptions and unsubscribe on shutdown. No `.Result` or `.Wait()` on async methods. Pass `ct` by name.
- Do not invent members. If unsure, read `Bitvavo.Net/Interfaces/Clients/**` or `docs/ai-api-map.md`.

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package Bitvavo.Net
```

## Usings

Samples omit usings and assume `ImplicitUsings` (System, System.Linq, System.Threading, System.Threading.Tasks) with top-level statements. `apiKey`, `apiSecret`, `credentials`, `configuration`, `request` and `services` stand for your own values. The usual set:

```csharp
using Bitvavo.Net;                         // BitvavoCredentials, BitvavoEnvironment
using Bitvavo.Net.Clients;                 // BitvavoRestClient, BitvavoSocketClient
using Bitvavo.Net.Enums;                   // OrderSide, OrderType, TimeInForce, KlineInterval, TriggerReference, ...
using Bitvavo.Net.Extensions;              // services.AddBitvavo(...)
using Bitvavo.Net.Interfaces.Clients;      // IBitvavoRestClient, IBitvavoSocketClient, IBitvavoSharedApiClient
using Bitvavo.Net.Interfaces.Clients.SpotApi;   // IBitvavoRestClientSpotSharedApi, IBitvavoSocketClientSpotSharedApi
using Bitvavo.Net.Objects.Internal;        // BitvavoExchange, BitvavoRateLimiters (public types in a namespace called Internal)
using Bitvavo.Net.Objects.Models.Spot;     // BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest, BitvavoOrder, ...
using Bitvavo.Net.Objects.Options;         // BitvavoOptions, BitvavoRestOptions, BitvavoSocketOptions
using CryptoExchange.Net.Authentication;   // HMACCredential
using CryptoExchange.Net.Objects;          // HttpResult<T>, WebSocketResult<T>, Error, RateLimitingBehaviour
using CryptoExchange.Net.Objects.Errors;   // ErrorType
using CryptoExchange.Net.Objects.Sockets;  // UpdateSubscription, DataEvent<T>
using CryptoExchange.Net.RateLimiting;     // RateLimitAdmission
using CryptoExchange.Net.SharedApis;       // Shared API types
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
```

## Main API surface

```text
BitvavoRestClient (IBitvavoRestClient)
  .SpotApi (IBitvavoRestClientSpotApi)
    .ExchangeData      public market data
    .Account           info, balances, fees, staking balance, ledger, cancel-on-disconnect
    .Trading           place, update, get, cancel, cancel all, atomic cancel, open orders, history, own trades
    .Funding           deposit address, deposit and withdrawal history, withdraw, crypto withdraw
    .Report            MiCA trade and book reports (public)
    .Institutional     subaccounts, transfers, per-subaccount queries
    .SharedApi         Shared API V2 (32 capabilities)
    .SharedClient      Shared API V1 (legacy interfaces, same instance)

BitvavoSocketClient (IBitvavoSocketClient)
  .SpotApi (IBitvavoSocketClientSpotApi)
    .ExchangeData      candles, trades (public)
    .Account           order events, fill events (private account channel)
    .SharedApi         Shared API V2 (klines, trades, spot orders, user trades)
    .SharedClient      Shared API V1 (same instance)

IBitvavoSharedApiClient     SpotRest + SpotSocket + GetCapability<T>() + Discover()
```

## Quick start 1 — REST, public data

```csharp
using var client = new BitvavoRestClient();

// Markets: status, tick size, decimals, order limits
var markets = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetMarketsAsync();
if (!markets.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{markets.Error?.ErrorType}: {markets.Error?.Message}");
    return;
}

foreach (var m in markets.Data.Where(x => x.Status == BitvavoMarketStatus.Trading).Take(5))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{m.Market} tick={m.TickSize} qtyDecimals={m.QuantityDecimals} minBase={m.MinOrderInBaseAsset} minQuote={m.MinOrderInQuoteAsset}");
}

// 24 h ticker of one market (weight 1; without a market weight 25). A market filter returns a collection of one:
// Bitvavo answers a single JSON object and the library reads it into IEnumerable<BitvavoTicker24h>.
var ticker = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetTicker24hAsync("BTC-EUR");
var t = ticker.Success ? ticker.Data.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Market == "BTC-EUR") : null;
Console.WriteLine($"last={t?.Last} bid={t?.Bid} ask={t?.Ask} volume={t?.Volume}");

// Order book snapshot, 5 levels per side
var book = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetOrderBookAsync("BTC-EUR", depth: 5);
if (book.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"nonce={book.Data.Nonce} bid={book.Data.Bids.FirstOrDefault()?.Price} ask={book.Data.Asks.FirstOrDefault()?.Price}");
}

// 24 hourly candles, newest first
var candles = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetKlinesAsync("BTC-EUR", KlineInterval.OneHour, limit: 24);
if (candles.Success)
{
    foreach (var k in candles.Data)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{k.OpenTime:u} O={k.OpenPrice} H={k.HighPrice} L={k.LowPrice} C={k.ClosePrice} V={k.Volume}");
    }
}
```

More public calls: `GetTickerPricesAsync(market?)` (last price), `GetTickerBookAsync(market?)` (best bid and ask, weight 1 — use it instead of a WebSocket ticker, which does not exist here), `GetPublicTradesAsync(market, limit?, startTime?, endTime?, tradeIdFrom?, tradeIdTo?)` (weight 5, window at most 24 h), `GetAssetsAsync(symbol?)`, `GetServerTimeAsync()`.

## Quick start 2 — REST, signed

```csharp
using var client = new BitvavoRestClient(o => o.ApiCredentials = new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret));

// Balances (weight 5). Available + InOrder = total.
var balances = await client.SpotApi.Account.GetBalancesAsync();
if (balances.Success)
{
    foreach (var b in balances.Data)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{b.Symbol} available={b.Available} inOrder={b.InOrder}");
    }
}

// Fee tier of a market: fractions, 0.0015 = 0.15 %
var fees = await client.SpotApi.Account.GetTradingFeesAsync(market: "ETH-EUR");
if (fees.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"maker={fees.Data.Maker:P3} taker={fees.Data.Taker:P3}");
}

const long operatorId = 1;                       // integer that identifies the trader or bot; required on every order operation
var clientOrderId = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();   // UUID, unique per market

// Place a post-only limit buy
var placed = await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(
    Market: "ETH-EUR",
    Side: OrderSide.Buy,
    OrderType: OrderType.Limit,
    OperatorId: operatorId,
    Amount: 0.01m,
    Price: 1500.00m,
    TimeInForce: TimeInForce.GoodTillCanceled,
    PostOnly: true,
    ClientOrderId: clientOrderId));
if (!placed.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{placed.Error?.ErrorType} code={placed.Error?.ErrorCode}: {placed.Error?.Message}");
    return;
}

var order = placed.Data;
Console.WriteLine($"{order.OrderId} {order.Status} remaining={order.AmountRemaining}");

// Read it back, by order id or by client order id
var byId = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOrderAsync("ETH-EUR", orderId: order.OrderId);
var byClientId = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOrderAsync("ETH-EUR", clientOrderId: clientOrderId);

// Change the price (limit and untriggered trigger orders only)
var updated = await client.SpotApi.Trading.UpdateOrderAsync(new BitvavoUpdateOrderRequest(
    Market: "ETH-EUR", OperatorId: operatorId, OrderId: order.OrderId, Price: 1499.50m));

// Cancel it
var cancelled = await client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrderAsync("ETH-EUR", operatorId, orderId: order.OrderId);
```

Other order shapes, all through `BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest`:

```csharp
// Market buy sized by a quote budget (25 EUR). Amount and AmountQuote are mutually exclusive.
await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(
    "ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Buy, OrderType.Market, operatorId, AmountQuote: 25m));

// Market sell sized in the base asset
await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(
    "ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Sell, OrderType.Market, operatorId, Amount: 0.01m));

// Stop-loss limit: waits in status AwaitingTrigger until the trigger price is reached, then places a limit order
await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(
    "ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Sell, OrderType.StopLossLimit, operatorId,
    Amount: 0.01m, Price: 1390m, TriggerAmount: 1400m,
    TriggerType: TriggerType.Price, TriggerReference: TriggerReference.LastTrade));
```

Lists and bulk calls:

```csharp
var open = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOpenOrdersAsync("ETH-EUR");                    // weight 5; without a market weight 100
var history = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOrderHistoryAsync("ETH-EUR", limit: 50);    // weight 5; also lists still-open orders
var fills = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetUserTradesAsync("ETH-EUR", limit: 50);        // weight 5; window at most 24 h
var cancelAll = await client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrdersAsync(operatorId, "ETH-EUR");    // weight 25 with a market, 100 without
var atomic = await client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrdersAtomicAsync("ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Buy, operatorId); // weight 100
```

## Quick start 3 — WebSocket, public streams

```csharp
using var socketClient = new BitvavoSocketClient();

// One market, one interval. Each event carries an array of candles (usually one).
var candles = await socketClient.SpotApi.ExchangeData.SubscribeToKlineUpdatesAsync(
    "BTC-EUR",
    KlineInterval.OneMinute,
    update =>
    {
        var latest = update.Data.Candle.LastOrDefault();
        Console.WriteLine($"{update.Data.Market} {update.Data.Interval} close={latest?.ClosePrice}");
    });
if (!candles.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine(candles.Error);
    return;
}

// Several markets on one subscription: dispatch on update.Data.Market
var trades = await socketClient.SpotApi.ExchangeData.SubscribeToTradeUpdatesAsync(
    new[] { "BTC-EUR", "ETH-EUR" },
    update => Console.WriteLine($"{update.Data.Market} {update.Data.Side} {update.Data.Amount} @ {update.Data.Price}"));

Console.ReadLine();

// Close one subscription, or all of them
await socketClient.UnsubscribeAsync(candles.Data);
await socketClient.UnsubscribeAllAsync();
```

Public channels that exist: `candles` and `trades`. A WebSocket ticker, ticker24h or book channel does not exist in this library: poll REST (`GetTickerBookAsync`, `GetTicker24hAsync`, `GetOrderBookAsync`).

## Quick start 4 — WebSocket, private account channel

```csharp
using var socketClient = new BitvavoSocketClient(o => o.ApiCredentials = new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret));
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();

// Order state changes of the listed markets
var orders = await socketClient.SpotApi.Account.SubscribeToOrderUpdatesAsync(
    new[] { "ETH-EUR" },
    update => Console.WriteLine(
        $"order {update.Data.OrderId} {update.Data.Status} filled={update.Data.FilledAmount}/{update.Data.Amount} exec={update.Data.ExecutionType}"),
    cts.Token);

// Own fills of the listed markets
var fills = await socketClient.SpotApi.Account.SubscribeToFillUpdatesAsync(
    new[] { "ETH-EUR" },
    update => Console.WriteLine(
        $"fill {update.Data.FillId} {update.Data.Side} {update.Data.Amount} @ {update.Data.Price} fee={update.Data.Fee} {update.Data.FeeCurrency} taker={update.Data.Taker}"));

if (!orders.Success || !fills.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine(orders.Error ?? fills.Error);
}

Console.ReadLine();
cts.Cancel();   // closes the order subscription
```

- The channel emits `order` and `fill` events only. There are no balance events and no balance subscription: read balances with `Account.GetBalancesAsync`.
- The channel is subscribed per market; `markets` is required. Both members share Bitvavo's `account` channel and differ by the event type they route.
- The library sends Bitvavo's `authenticate` action (key, HMAC-SHA256 of `timestamp + "GET/v2/websocket"`, timestamp, window) before the first private subscribe on a connection. Without credentials the subscribe fails with `NoApiCredentialsError`.
- A subscribe counts as successful once it is sent: Bitvavo acknowledges subscribes only in an aggregated event. A wrong market name is not reported through `Success`, and Bitvavo `error` events are not routed. Validate market names against `GetMarketsAsync`.
- Bitvavo gives no ordering guarantee between the `order` event and the `fill` event of one trade. After a reconnect, read the state back over REST (`GetOpenOrdersAsync`, `GetUserTradesAsync`).
- `DataEvent<T>`: `update.Data`, `update.ReceiveTime`, `update.Symbol`, `update.StreamId`, `update.OriginalData`.

## Quick start 5 — dependency injection

```csharp
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddLogging();

// One options object for the whole library: credentials reach REST and socket
services.AddBitvavo((BitvavoOptions o) =>
{
    o.ApiCredentials = new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret);
    o.Rest.RequestTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
    o.Rest.AutoTimestamp = true;
    o.SharedApi.PreferredTransport = SharedTransport.Rest;
});

await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();
var rest = provider.GetRequiredService<IBitvavoRestClient>();
var socket = provider.GetRequiredService<IBitvavoSocketClient>();
var shared = provider.GetRequiredService<IBitvavoSharedApiClient>();
```

Constructor injection:

```csharp
public sealed class OrderService(IBitvavoRestClient rest)
{
    public async Task<string?> BuyAsync(string market, decimal amount, decimal price, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var result = await rest.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(
            new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(market, OrderSide.Buy, OrderType.Limit, OperatorId: 1,
                Amount: amount, Price: price, ClientOrderId: Guid.NewGuid().ToString()),
            ct);
        return result.Success ? result.Data.OrderId : null;
    }
}
```

The three registrations, exactly:

```csharp
// 1) Legacy overload: optional Action<BitvavoRestOptions> and Action<BitvavoSocketOptions>
services.AddBitvavo();
services.AddBitvavo(
    restOptionsDelegate: o => { o.ApiCredentials = credentials; o.AutoTimestamp = true; },
    socketOptionsDelegate: o => o.ApiCredentials = credentials);

// 2) From configuration, for example the section "Bitvavo" of appsettings.json
services.AddBitvavo(configuration.GetSection("Bitvavo"));

// 3) Library-wide options (explicit lambda type)
services.AddBitvavo((BitvavoOptions o) => o.ApiCredentials = credentials);
```

appsettings.json for registration 2 (keys are relative to the bound section; the environment name ignores case, an unknown name throws at registration):

```json
{
  "Bitvavo": {
    "Environment": { "Name": "Live" },
    "ApiCredentials": { "Spot": { "Key": "your-key", "Secret": "your-secret" } },
    "Rest": { "RequestTimeout": "00:00:10", "ReceiveWindowMs": 10000 },
    "Socket": { "ReceiveWindowMs": 10000 },
    "SharedApi": { "PreferredTransport": "Rest" }
  }
}
```

Lifetimes and behaviour:

- `IBitvavoRestClient` is transient, on a typed `HttpClient` whose timeout is `RequestTimeout`. `IBitvavoRestClientSpotApi` is transient.
- `IBitvavoSocketClient` is a singleton (one shared WebSocket pool) unless `BitvavoOptions.SocketClientLifeTime` is set (library-wide overload only). `IBitvavoSocketClientSpotApi` follows it.
- Every overload registers options through the options pipeline, so an application `PostConfigure` runs last and wins:

```csharp
services.PostConfigure<BitvavoRestOptions>(o => o.RateLimitingBehaviour = RateLimitingBehaviour.Fail);
services.PostConfigure<BitvavoSocketOptions>(o => o.SocketNoDataTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
```

- Also resolvable: `IBitvavoSharedApiClient`, `IBitvavoRestClientSpotSharedApi`, `IBitvavoSocketClientSpotSharedApi` and every Shared capability interface (V2 and V1).
- Trap: `services.AddBitvavo(o => o.ApiCredentials = credentials)` binds the REST overload (language version C# 13 and later; at C# 12, the net8.0 default, the library-wide overload is picked and both clients get the credentials) and the socket client gets NO credentials. For both transports write `(BitvavoOptions o) => ...` as in registration 3, or use both delegates of registration 1. A lambda that touches `Rest`, `Socket`, `SharedApi` or `SocketClientLifeTime` binds the library-wide overload by itself.

## Quick start 6 — Shared API client, `GetCapability`

The Shared API is CryptoExchange.Net's exchange-independent contract. Each capability is its own interface; `Discover()` lists what Bitvavo registers; transport preference decides which transport answers when both could.

```csharp
async Task Run(IBitvavoSharedApiClient shared)
{
    var info = shared.Discover();                      // capabilities per transport

    // Lookup by capability type; null when Bitvavo does not register it
    var klines = shared.GetCapability<IGetKlines>();
    if (klines is null)
    {
        return;
    }

    var result = await klines.Capability.GetKlinesAsync(
        new GetKlinesRequest(new SharedSymbol(TradingMode.Spot, "ETH", "EUR"), SharedKlineInterval.OneHour, limit: 24));
    if (result.Success)
    {
        foreach (var kline in result.Data)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"{kline.OpenTime:g} close={kline.ClosePrice}");
        }
    }
}
```

`GetCapability<T>(SharedTransport? transport = null)` returns a lookup result (`Capability`, `Transport`, `Exchange`, `Options`) or null. The transport-neutral interfaces (`IGetKlines`) answer `IExchangeCallResult<T>`; the REST twins (`IGetKlinesRest`) answer `HttpResult<T>`. A typed lookup reference selects the REST twin:

```csharp
var klinesRest = shared.GetCapability(SharedCapabilities.Klines.GetKlines.Rest);   // null when not registered
var restResult = klinesRest is null
    ? null
    : await klinesRest.Capability.GetKlinesAsync(new GetKlinesRequest(new SharedSymbol(TradingMode.Spot, "ETH", "EUR"), SharedKlineInterval.OneHour, limit: 24));
```

To skip the lookup, use the typed Shared object directly (`shared` is the `IBitvavoSharedApiClient` resolved in Quick start 5):

```csharp
IBitvavoRestClientSpotSharedApi api = shared.SpotRest;   // or restClient.SpotApi.SharedApi

var symbol = new SharedSymbol(TradingMode.Spot, "ETH", "EUR");      // market ETH-EUR
var operatorParameter = new ExchangeParameters(
    new ExchangeParameter(BitvavoExchange.ExchangeName, "OperatorId", 1L));   // value type is long: 1L

var placed = await api.PlaceSpotOrderAsync(new PlaceSpotOrderRequest(
    symbol,
    SharedOrderSide.Buy,
    SharedOrderType.Limit,
    SharedQuantity.Base(0.01m),
    price: 1500m,
    timeInForce: SharedTimeInForce.GoodTillCanceled,
    clientOrderId: api.GenerateClientOrderId(),          // a UUID
    exchangeParameters: operatorParameter));
if (!placed.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine(placed.Error);
    return;
}

var order = await api.GetSpotOrderAsync(new GetOrderRequest(symbol, placed.Data.Id));
var cancelled = await api.CancelSpotOrderAsync(new CancelOrderRequest(symbol, placed.Data.Id, operatorParameter));

// Or set the operator id once for every request of this exchange
api.SetDefaultExchangeParameter("OperatorId", 1L);
// ... and later: api.ResetDefaultExchangeParameters();
```

Exchange parameters Bitvavo needs (the Shared requests have no field for them), keyed by exchange `BitvavoExchange.ExchangeName` ("Bitvavo"):

| Name | Value type | Needed by |
|---|---|---|
| `OperatorId` | `long`, required | place, cancel, cancel by client id, cancel all, cancel all of a symbol, edit, edit by client id, place trigger order, cancel trigger order |
| `Markets` | `string[]`, required | `SubscribeToSpotOrderUpdatesAsync`, `SubscribeToUserTradeUpdatesAsync` (the account channel is subscribed per market) |
| `TriggerReference` | `TriggerReference` enum, optional (default `LastTrade`) | `PlaceSpotTriggerOrderAsync` |

A request that lacks a required parameter is rejected with `ArgumentError` before anything is sent. Wrong value type: use `1L`, not `1`.

Trigger orders (Bitvavo has no trigger endpoint: a trigger order is an ordinary stop-loss or take-profit order that waits in `AwaitingTrigger`):

```csharp
var triggerParameters = new ExchangeParameters(
    new ExchangeParameter(BitvavoExchange.ExchangeName, "OperatorId", 1L),
    new ExchangeParameter(BitvavoExchange.ExchangeName, "TriggerReference", TriggerReference.BestBid));

// Sell 0.01 ETH when the price falls to 1400; with a limit price (1390) the placed order is a limit order, without it a market order
var stop = await api.PlaceSpotTriggerOrderAsync(new PlaceSpotTriggerOrderRequest(
    symbol, SharedTriggerPriceDirection.PriceBelow, 1400m, SharedOrderSide.Sell, SharedQuantity.Base(0.01m), 1390m, triggerParameters));
```

Mapping (assumed, not measured against the live API): sell + `PriceBelow` = stop loss, sell + `PriceAbove` = take profit, buy + `PriceAbove` = stop loss, buy + `PriceBelow` = take profit; with a limit price the `...Limit` order type. Quantity in the quote asset is only valid without a limit price.

Paging through Shared history (`NextPageRequest` of the result is the token of the next call):

```csharp
PageRequest? next = null;
do
{
    var page = await api.GetClosedSpotOrdersAsync(new GetClosedOrdersRequest(symbol), next);
    if (!page.Success)
    {
        break;
    }

    foreach (var closed in page.Data)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{closed.OrderId} {closed.Status}");
    }

    next = page.NextPageRequest;
} while (next is not null);
```

Shared WebSocket (V2). The private ones need the `Markets` exchange parameter:

```csharp
IBitvavoSocketClientSpotSharedApi sockets = shared.SpotSocket;   // or socketClient.SpotApi.SharedApi

var klineSub = await sockets.SubscribeToKlineUpdatesAsync(
    new SubscribeKlineRequest(symbol, SharedKlineInterval.OneMinute),      // one symbol only
    update => Console.WriteLine($"{update.Data.OpenTime:T} close={update.Data.ClosePrice}"));

var tradeSub = await sockets.SubscribeToTradeUpdatesAsync(
    new SubscribeTradeRequest(symbol),                                     // several symbols allowed
    update => { foreach (var trade in update.Data) Console.WriteLine($"{trade.Symbol} {trade.Price}"); });

var marketsParameter = new ExchangeParameters(
    new ExchangeParameter(BitvavoExchange.ExchangeName, "Markets", new[] { "ETH-EUR" }));

var orderSub = await sockets.SubscribeToSpotOrderUpdatesAsync(
    new SubscribeSpotOrderRequest(marketsParameter),
    update => { foreach (var o in update.Data) Console.WriteLine($"{o.Symbol} {o.OrderId} {o.Status}"); });

var userTradeSub = await sockets.SubscribeToUserTradeUpdatesAsync(
    new SubscribeUserTradeRequest(exchangeParameters: marketsParameter),
    update => { foreach (var u in update.Data) Console.WriteLine($"{u.Symbol} {u.Side} {u.Price}"); });

await sockets.UnsubscribeAllAsync();
```

REST V2 capabilities (32): `IGetAssetRest`, `IGetAllAssetsRest`, `IGetKlinesRest`, `IGetBalancesRest`, `IGetFeesRest`, `IGetLedgerRest`, `IGetDepositAddressesRest`, `IGetDepositHistoryRest`, `IGetWithdrawalHistoryRest`, `IWithdrawRest`, `IPlaceSpotOrderRest`, `IGetSpotOrderRest`, `IGetSpotOrderByClientOrderIdRest`, `IGetOpenSpotOrdersRest`, `IGetClosedSpotOrdersRest`, `IGetSpotOrderTradesRest`, `IGetSpotUserTradeHistoryRest`, `ICancelSpotOrderRest`, `ICancelSpotOrderByClientOrderIdRest`, `IGetSpotSymbolsRest`, `IGetTickerRest`, `IGetAllTickersRest`, `IGetOrderBookRest`, `IGetBookTickerRest`, `IGetRecentTradesRest`, `ICancelAllSpotOrdersRest`, `ICancelAllSpotSymbolOrdersRest`, `IEditSpotOrderRest`, `IEditSpotOrderByClientOrderIdRest`, `IPlaceSpotTriggerOrderRest`, `IGetSpotTriggerOrderRest`, `ICancelSpotTriggerOrderRest`. WebSocket V2 (4): `ISubscribeKlinesSocket`, `ISubscribeTradesSocket`, `ISubscribeSpotOrdersSocket`, `ISubscribeUserTradesSocket`. Legacy V1 aggregates (same instance): `IBitvavoRestClientSpotApiShared` (14 interfaces) and `IBitvavoSocketClientSpotApiShared` (4), reached through `SpotApi.SharedClient`. Batch orders are absent: Bitvavo has no endpoint.

Shared behaviour worth knowing:
- Order types: `Limit`, `Market`, `LimitMaker` (limit + post-only). `SharedOrderType.Other` throws `ArgumentException` on place. Time in force: GTC, IOC, FOK. Limit orders take the quantity in the base asset; market orders take base or quote (`SharedQuantity.Base(x)`, `SharedQuantity.Quote(x)`).
- The by-client-id capabilities (`GetSpotOrderByClientOrderIdAsync`, `CancelSpotOrderByClientOrderIdAsync`, `EditSpotOrderByClientOrderIdAsync`) carry the client order id in the request's `OrderId` field.
- Edit (`EditOrderRequest`): the new total quantity and/or the new price, at least one; a market order cannot be edited.
- `CancelAllSpotOrdersAsync` (weight 100) and `CancelAllSpotSymbolOrdersAsync` (weight 25) return no order ids.
- Closed orders: Bitvavo's history also lists open orders; they are dropped, so a page can be shorter than the limit.
- Ledger: max 100 transactions per page, paged by page number; a trade is two entries sharing a `RelationId`; fees are not separate entries; the asset filter is applied per fetched page.
- Deposit addresses: a request that names a network is rejected (one address per asset); fiat assets give an empty list. Withdraw: network required, network fee charged on top, id returned is Bitvavo's withdrawal id.
- Kline intervals: 13 (`SharedKlineInterval` OneMinute to OneMonth, no ThreeMinutes), at most 1440 per request. Order book 1–1000 levels, `Nonce` is the sequence number.
- Symbols: `GetSpotSymbolsAsync` fills a process-wide symbol cache behind `SpotSymbolCatalog`. The price grid is `PriceStep` and `PriceDecimals`, derived from `tickSize`.

## Intent to method map

REST (`client` = `BitvavoRestClient`; HTTP and weight in `docs/ai-api-map.md`):

```text
Markets, tick sizes, limits ....... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetMarketsAsync()
Candles ........................... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetKlinesAsync("BTC-EUR", KlineInterval.OneHour, limit: 24)
Server time ....................... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetServerTimeAsync()
Assets and networks ............... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetAssetsAsync()
Last price ........................ client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetTickerPricesAsync("BTC-EUR")
Best bid and ask .................. client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetTickerBookAsync("BTC-EUR")
24 h ticker ....................... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetTicker24hAsync("BTC-EUR")
Order book ........................ client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetOrderBookAsync("BTC-EUR", depth: 10)
Public trades ..................... client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetPublicTradesAsync("BTC-EUR")
Account info and fee tier ......... client.SpotApi.Account.GetAccountInfoAsync()
Balances .......................... client.SpotApi.Account.GetBalancesAsync()
Fee tier of a market .............. client.SpotApi.Account.GetTradingFeesAsync(market: "ETH-EUR")
Staking balance ................... client.SpotApi.Account.GetStakingBalanceAsync()
Ledger ............................ client.SpotApi.Account.GetTransactionHistoryAsync(page: 1, maxItems: 100)
Cancel-on-disconnect .............. client.SpotApi.Account.ResetCancelOnDisconnectAsync(codGroupId: 1, expiryAfterSeconds: 30)
Place order ....................... client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(...))
Update order ...................... client.SpotApi.Trading.UpdateOrderAsync(new BitvavoUpdateOrderRequest(...))
Get order ......................... client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOrderAsync("ETH-EUR", orderId: id)
Cancel order ...................... client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrderAsync("ETH-EUR", operatorId, orderId: id)
Cancel all ........................ client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrdersAsync(operatorId, "ETH-EUR")
Atomic cancel one side ............ client.SpotApi.Trading.CancelOrdersAtomicAsync("ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Buy, operatorId)
Open orders ....................... client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOpenOrdersAsync("ETH-EUR")
Order history ..................... client.SpotApi.Trading.GetOrderHistoryAsync("ETH-EUR")
Own trades ........................ client.SpotApi.Trading.GetUserTradesAsync("ETH-EUR")
Deposit address ................... client.SpotApi.Funding.GetDepositAddressAsync("BTC")
Deposit history ................... client.SpotApi.Funding.GetDepositHistoryAsync()
Withdrawal history ................ client.SpotApi.Funding.GetWithdrawalHistoryAsync()

Subaccount order cancellation ..... client.SpotApi.Institutional.CancelSubaccountOrderAsync(...) / CancelSubaccountOrdersAsync(operatorId)
```

WebSocket (`socketClient` = `BitvavoSocketClient`):

```text

Public trades ..................... socketClient.SpotApi.ExchangeData.SubscribeToTradeUpdatesAsync("BTC-EUR", handler)
Public trades, many markets ....... socketClient.SpotApi.ExchangeData.SubscribeToTradeUpdatesAsync(new[] { "BTC-EUR", "ETH-EUR" }, handler)
Own order events .................. socketClient.SpotApi.Account.SubscribeToOrderUpdatesAsync(new[] { "ETH-EUR" }, handler)
Own fills ......................... socketClient.SpotApi.Account.SubscribeToFillUpdatesAsync(new[] { "ETH-EUR" }, handler)
```

## Markets, sizing and the price grid

```csharp
var markets = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetMarketsAsync();
var eth = markets.Success ? markets.Data.FirstOrDefault(m => m.Market == "ETH-EUR") : null;
if (eth is null || eth.Status != BitvavoMarketStatus.Trading)
{
    return;   // order only while the market is in status Trading
}

var tick = eth.TickSize ?? 0.01m;
var price = Math.Floor(1503.987m / tick) * tick;                                     // a multiple of tickSize, or error 422
var amount = Math.Round(0.0123456789m, eth.QuantityDecimals ?? 8, MidpointRounding.ToZero);   // quantityDecimals decimals of base asset
```

- `MinOrderInBaseAsset`, `MinOrderInQuoteAsset`, `MaxOrderInBaseAsset`, `MaxOrderInQuoteAsset` are strings: parse with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`; an empty string means no figure.
- `QuantityDecimals` limits the decimals of `Amount`; `NotionalDecimals` those of `AmountQuote`; a value with too many decimals is rejected with code 429 (`ErrorType.InvalidParameter`). A price with more than 15 decimals is code 215.
- `BitvavoMarket.PricePrecision` is an `int?` and null on every market the live API lists. The price grid is `TickSize`.
- `MaxOpenOrders` is the per-market figure (the live API returns 100, 200, 400 or null); Bitvavo's error table names 100 open orders per market as the limit (code 235, `ErrorType.RateLimitOrder`).
- `BitvavoMarketStatus`: `Trading`, `Halted` (no create, update or cancel), `Auction` (no market orders, no matching), `AuctionMatching` (opening price is calculated), `CancelOnly` (cancels only). Interacting with a market that is not in trading status can fail with codes 423–426 or 431 (`UnavailableSymbol`, transient).

## Order lifecycle

- A new order starts as `OrderStatus.New`, or `AwaitingTrigger` for stop-loss and take-profit types (it moves to `New` under the same order id when it fires).
- Active: `New`, `AwaitingTrigger`, `PartiallyFilled` (update or cancel possible). Completed: `Filled`, `Expired` (a market order without liquidity or balance, or IOC/FOK that could not execute), `Canceled`, `CanceledAuction`, `CanceledSelfTradePrevention`, `CanceledIoc`, `CanceledFok`, `CanceledMarketProtection`, `CanceledPostOnly`, `Rejected`.
- Why an order was cancelled or reduced: `BitvavoOrder.RestatementReason` (string, for example `cancelOnDisconnect`, `cancelOnSelfTradePrevention`, `cancelPostOnly`).
- Track state with the private `order` and `fill` events, and read back over REST for certainty: `GetOrderAsync(market, orderId:)`, or by `clientOrderId:`.
- `BitvavoOrder.Fills` lists the fills embedded in an order (`BitvavoFill`); `Fee` and `FeeCurrency` are absent while a fill is not settled.
- Self-trade prevention: `SelfTradePrevention` on place (`DecrementAndCancel`, `CancelOldest`, `CancelNewest`, `CancelBoth`).
- Market protection cancels orders that would execute far from the market price; `DisableMarketProtection: true` on place switches it off for that order.

## Cancel on disconnect

Server-side dead-man switch: Bitvavo cancels every open order of a group when no `cancelOrdersAfter` arrives before the timer expires.

```csharp
// 1) Create the group (codGroupId 1) with a 30 s timer. Minimum 10 s; 0 removes the group. Bitvavo allows one group by default.
var group = await client.SpotApi.Account.ResetCancelOnDisconnectAsync(codGroupId: 1, expiryAfterSeconds: 30);
Console.WriteLine(group.Success ? $"expires at unix {group.Data.TimeOfExpirySeconds}" : group.Error?.ToString());

// 2) Place orders in the group (not for market orders)
await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(new BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest(
    "ETH-EUR", OrderSide.Buy, OrderType.Limit, OperatorId: 1, Amount: 0.01m, Price: 1500m, CodGroupId: 1));

// 3) Heartbeat at half the timer (every 15 s for a 30 s timer)
using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15));
while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync())
{
    await client.SpotApi.Account.ResetCancelOnDisconnectAsync(codGroupId: 1, expiryAfterSeconds: 30);
}
```

The heartbeat is documented at weight 5 and is deliberately never counted or refused by the client-side rate limiter: a refused heartbeat would let the timer expire. Bitvavo's failure code for a group problem is 433; it is not in the error table, so it maps to `ErrorType.Unknown`.

## History and pagination

The typed API does not paginate for you.

```csharp
// Own trades: Bitvavo serves a window of at most 24 h per request. Walk backwards one day at a time.
var end = DateTime.UtcNow;
for (var day = 0; day < 7; day++)
{
    var start = end.AddHours(-24);
    var trades = await client.SpotApi.Trading.GetUserTradesAsync("ETH-EUR", limit: 1000, startTime: start, endTime: end);
    if (!trades.Success)
    {
        break;
    }

    foreach (var fill in trades.Data)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{fill.Timestamp:u} {fill.Side} {fill.Amount} @ {fill.Price} fee={fill.Fee} {fill.FeeCurrency}");
    }

    end = start;
}

// Ledger: page number based
var pageNumber = 1;
while (true)
{
    var ledger = await client.SpotApi.Account.GetTransactionHistoryAsync(page: pageNumber, maxItems: 100);
    if (!ledger.Success)
    {
        break;
    }

    foreach (var entry in ledger.Data.Items)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{entry.ExecutedAt:u} {entry.Type} sent={entry.SentAmount} {entry.SentCurrency} received={entry.ReceivedAmount} {entry.ReceivedCurrency}");
    }

    if (ledger.Data.CurrentPage >= ledger.Data.TotalPages)
    {
        break;
    }

    pageNumber++;
}
```

- Cursors: `startTime` / `endTime` (wire `start`, `end`), `tradeIdFrom` / `tradeIdTo`, `orderIdFrom` / `orderIdTo`, `page` / `maxItems`. Histories return 1–1000 entries (default 500); Bitvavo describes them as latest to earliest (not measured live for every list); ledger `maxItems` 1–100.
- Candles: `limit` 1–1440; `startTime` and `endTime` must align with the interval boundary (Bitvavo).
- `GetUserTradesAsync(..., tradeId)`: Bitvavo documents `tradeId` as deprecated (read as `tradeIdTo`); prefer `tradeIdFrom` / `tradeIdTo`.

## Funding

```csharp
var address = await client.SpotApi.Funding.GetDepositAddressAsync("BTC");   // crypto: Address (+ PaymentReference); fiat: Iban, Bic, Description

// Networks of an asset come from the asset data
var assets = await client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetAssetsAsync("BTC");
var networks = assets.Success ? assets.Data.First().Networks : Array.Empty<string>();

// Crypto withdrawal: the network is required; the fee is charged on top unless DeductFeeFromAmount is true.
// The address must be verified in the account's address book. The IdempotencyKey makes a retry safe.
var withdrawal = await client.SpotApi.Funding.WithdrawCryptoAsync(new BitvavoCryptoWithdrawRequest(
    Asset: "BTC",
    Network: "Bitcoin",
    Address: "bc1q...",
    Amount: 0.001m,
    DeductFeeFromAmount: false,
    IdempotencyKey: Guid.NewGuid().ToString()));

// Older endpoint (address or IBAN, optional internal transfer between Bitvavo accounts)
await client.SpotApi.Funding.WithdrawAsync(new BitvavoWithdrawRequest("EUR", 100m, "NL00BANK0123456789"));
```

Withdrawals move funds. Bitvavo disables 2FA and the e-mail address confirmation for API withdrawals: the API key's `withdraw` permission is the only gate. Withdrawal history status values: `awaiting_processing`, `awaiting_email_confirmation`, `awaiting_bitvavo_inspection`, `approved`, `sending`, `in_mempool`, `processed`, `completed`, `canceled`.

## Institutional (subaccounts)

Needs the main account's key with `Include all subaccounts`, `Internal Transfer` and `Administrative`.

```csharp
var sub = await client.SpotApi.Institutional.CreateSubaccountAsync("bot-1");
if (sub.Success)
{
    var transfer = await client.SpotApi.Institutional.CreateTransferAsync(new BitvavoCreateTransferRequest(
        SubaccountId: sub.Data.Id,
        Direction: SubaccountTransferDirection.MasterToSub,
        Symbol: "EUR",
        Amount: 100m,
        ClientRequestId: Guid.NewGuid().ToString()));

    var balances = await client.SpotApi.Institutional.GetSubaccountBalancesAsync(subaccountId: sub.Data.Id);
}
```

The rate limit budget is shared between the main account and its subaccounts.

## Error handling

Bitvavo, network and rate-limit failures come back as `result.Error`; exceptions are for misuse.

```csharp
var result = await client.SpotApi.Trading.PlaceOrderAsync(request);
if (!result.Success)
{
    var error = result.Error!;
    Console.WriteLine($"{error.ErrorType} code={error.ErrorCode} transient={error.IsTransient}: {error.Message}");

    switch (error.ErrorType)
    {
        case ErrorType.InsufficientBalance:          // 216, 408
        case ErrorType.InvalidQuantity:              // 210, 212, 217, 406
            break;
        case ErrorType.InvalidPrice:                 // 211, 213, 215, 422 (not on the tick size)
            break;
        case ErrorType.DuplicateClientOrderId:       // 220: the clientOrderId already exists in this market
            break;
        case ErrorType.UnknownOrder:                 // 240
            break;
        case ErrorType.Timeout when error.ErrorCode == "109":
            // The request timed out and the order may or may not exist: read it back by clientOrderId before retrying.
            break;
        case ErrorType.RateLimitRequest:             // 105, 112
            break;
    }
}
```

`Error` members: `ErrorType`, `ErrorCode` (string: Bitvavo's `errorCode`), `Code`, `Message`, `IsTransient`, `Exception`.

Bitvavo code to `ErrorType` (an unlisted code gives `ErrorType.Unknown`; the table is `BitvavoErrors.SpotMapping`, internal):

```text
InvalidParameter            no   102 200 201 204 205 206 236 239 429 439 510
MissingParameter            no   203 232
RejectedOrderConfiguration  no   202 231 234
InvalidQuantity             no   210 212 217 406
InvalidPrice                no   211 213 215 422
InsufficientBalance         no   216 408
UnknownSymbol               no   219
DuplicateClientOrderId      no   220
RateLimitOrder              no   235          (more than 100 open orders in the market)
InvalidStopParameters       no   237 238
UnknownOrder                no   240
UnavailableSymbol           yes  423 424 425 426 431   (market not in trading status)
InvalidOperation            no   401 407 410 411 412 413 415 514
InvalidOperation            yes  405 414      (withdrawal not possible yet)
Unauthorized                no   301 305-314 316-320 322 402 403 409 511 512 513
RiskError                   no   434 435 436 437 438
SystemError                 yes  101 107 108 111 400 404 419
MissingCredentials          no   300
InvalidTimestamp            no   302 303 304
RateLimitRequest            yes  105 112
Timeout                     no   109          (verify the state before retrying)
Timeout                     yes  430
```

- Code 429 is an HTTP 400 about too many decimals; it is unrelated to HTTP 429 (rate limit), which carries 105 or 112.
- HTTP 429 keeps Bitvavo's code and message on a `ServerRateLimitError`. Bitvavo sends no `Retry-After`, and the library does not back off by itself after a 429.
- Client-side errors: `ClientRateLimitError` (limiter refusal under `RateLimitingBehaviour.Fail`, or a request that can never fit), `ArgumentError` (Shared request validation), `NoApiCredentialsError`, `CancellationRequestedError`.

Retry only what is transient. Never retry an order placement blindly:

```csharp
async Task<HttpResult<T>> WithRetry<T>(Func<Task<HttpResult<T>>> call, int maxAttempts = 3)
{
    HttpResult<T> last = default!;
    for (var attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++)
    {
        last = await call();
        if (last.Success || last.Error?.IsTransient != true)
        {
            return last;
        }

        await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500 * Math.Pow(2, attempt - 1)));   // Bitvavo: retry after 500 ms, then longer
    }

    return last;
}

var markets = await WithRetry(() => client.SpotApi.ExchangeData.GetMarketsAsync());
```

For `PlaceOrderAsync`, always send a `ClientOrderId`; after a failure that may have reached the exchange, call `GetOrderAsync(market, clientOrderId: id)` first. A duplicate `ClientOrderId` is answered with code 220.

## Rate limiting

- Bitvavo: 1000 weight points per minute. Signed requests count per account (all keys and subaccounts), public requests per IP address. Overrun → HTTP 429 code 105; blocked for 1 minute (signed) or 15 minutes (IP). Each WebSocket session allows 5000 messages per second (code 112); the weight budget is shared by all connections.
- The client counts every REST request against two separate sliding one-minute guards (signed, public), with the weight of each endpoint (most 1; balance, trades, histories 5; 24 h ticker without market 25; open orders and cancel all without market 100; atomic cancel 100; crypto withdrawal 25). Variable weights are passed per call. WebSocket frames are not counted. The cancel-on-disconnect heartbeat is never counted.
- Default `MaxUtilization` is 0.9 (90 % utilization): 10 % of each budget stays free for other processes on the same account or IP, so 900 points per minute are usable per budget. A request that would overrun waits (`RateLimitingBehaviour.Wait`, default behaviour) or fails with `ClientRateLimitError` (`Fail`).
- `BitvavoExchange.RateLimiter` is one static, settable `BitvavoRateLimiters` for the whole process (the budget belongs to the account or IP, not to a client). Set it at start-up; a replacement counts from zero.

```csharp
BitvavoExchange.RateLimiter = new BitvavoRateLimiters(maxUtilization: 0.8, weightPerMinute: 1000);

BitvavoExchange.RateLimiter.RateLimitTriggered += trigger =>
    Console.WriteLine($"limit hit: weight {trigger.RequestWeight}, current {trigger.Current}/{trigger.Limit}, wait {trigger.DelayTime}");
BitvavoExchange.RateLimiter.RateLimitUpdated += update =>
    Console.WriteLine($"usage {update.Current}/{update.Limit}");

// Fail fast instead of waiting
using var client = new BitvavoRestClient(o => o.RateLimitingBehaviour = RateLimitingBehaviour.Fail);

// Per-client ratio on top of MaxUtilization: the stricter wins
using var careful = new BitvavoRestClient(o => o.RateLimitAdmission = (_, _) => RateLimitAdmission.WithMaxUtilizationRatio(0.5));
```

- `BitvavoRateLimiters(double maxUtilization = 0.9, int weightPerMinute = 1000)`: `maxUtilization` must lie between `100 / weightPerMinute` (the heaviest request must fit) and 1; `weightPerMinute` must be at least 100. Otherwise `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- Cheaper calls: pass a market where one is optional (`GetOpenOrdersAsync("ETH-EUR")` 5 instead of 100, `GetTicker24hAsync("BTC-EUR")` 1 instead of 25), and prefer WebSocket subscriptions (candles, trades, order and fill events) over polling.

## Time sync (`AutoTimestamp`)

Signed requests carry `Bitvavo-Access-Timestamp` and `Bitvavo-Access-Window`; Bitvavo rejects a request that arrives outside the window (codes 302, 303, 304 → `ErrorType.InvalidTimestamp`).

```csharp
using var client = new BitvavoRestClient(o =>
{
    o.ApiCredentials = new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret);
    o.AutoTimestamp = true;       // measures the clock offset through the public GET /v2/time before the first signed request
    o.ReceiveWindowMs = 10_000;   // Bitvavo-Access-Window in ms: default 10000, Bitvavo maximum 60000
});
```

- The time request is public on purpose (a signed one would need the sync it performs), and a failing time request does not block the signed call. `TimestampRecalculationInterval` (CryptoExchange.Net option) sets how often the offset is measured again.
- `ReceiveWindowMs` exists on `BitvavoRestOptions` and `BitvavoSocketOptions`; the socket value is the `window` of the `authenticate` action. The socket `authenticate` timestamp comes from the same time source as REST signing.
- Raise `ReceiveWindowMs` or fix the clock when you see code 304.

## Credentials and rotation (`SetApiCredentials`)

```csharp
var credentials = new BitvavoCredentials(apiKey, apiSecret);                       // key + secret
var viaHmac = new BitvavoCredentials(new HMACCredential(apiKey, apiSecret));       // same thing
var empty = new BitvavoCredentials();                                              // public endpoints only

// Switch key on a live client: restClient / socketClient are an IBitvavoRestClient / IBitvavoSocketClient or the concrete classes
restClient.SetApiCredentials(new BitvavoCredentials(newKey, newSecret));
socketClient.SetApiCredentials(new BitvavoCredentials(newKey, newSecret));
```

- REST: the next signed request signs with the new key.
- Socket: a private subscription made afterwards authenticates with the new key on a connection of its own. The old key's connection stays open for the subscriptions it already carries. Setting the same key again keeps the connection. A public subscription made after a key change reuses the open connection. A reconnect authenticates again with the key held at that moment.
- `BitvavoCredentials.Copy()` is a deep copy. Never commit keys; read them from configuration or a secret store.
- Key permissions in Bitvavo: view, trade, withdraw (plus `Include all subaccounts`, `Internal Transfer`, `Administrative` for the institutional endpoints). Reading orders and trades needs view and trade together. Missing permission → codes 310, 311, 312, 511, 512, 513 (`ErrorType.Unauthorized`). When the key has an IP whitelist in Bitvavo, a request from another IP fails with code 307.

## WebSocket lifecycle

- One connection serves many channels; `SocketSubscriptionsCombineTarget` (default 10) subscriptions are combined per connection. Bitvavo sets no limit on connections; the rate limit is shared by all of them.
- The library reconnects and resubscribes automatically. `UpdateSubscription` events: `ConnectionLost`, `ConnectionRestored` (offline time), `ConnectionClosed`, `ResubscribingFailed`, `Exception`, `SubscriptionStatusChanged`, `ActivityPaused`, `ActivityUnpaused`.
- Close: cancel the `ct` you passed to the subscribe call, `await subscription.Data.CloseAsync()`, `await socketClient.UnsubscribeAsync(subscription.Data)`, or `await socketClient.UnsubscribeAllAsync()` at shutdown. Inspect: `socketClient.CurrentSubscriptions`, `socketClient.CurrentConnections`.
- A restart of Bitvavo's matching engine can reset the order-book `nonce`; WebSocket connections stay connected.
- Options on `BitvavoSocketOptions`: `ReceiveWindowMs`, `SocketSubscriptionsCombineTarget`, `SocketNoDataTimeout`, `ReconnectPolicy`, `ReconnectInterval`, `MaxSocketConnections`, `ApiCredentials`, `Environment`.

## Wire format

- Prices and amounts: JSON strings (`"amount":"0.5"`); responses parse into `decimal`. Sub-cent values with exponent notation (`1e-8`) parse too.
- `DateTime`: unix milliseconds. The nanosecond properties (`CreatedNs`, `UpdatedNs`, `TimestampNs`, `TimeNs`) hold unix nanoseconds as `long`.
- Enums: wire strings (`KlineInterval.OneWeek` = `1W`, `OneMonth` = `1M`, `OneMinute` = `1m`; `TimeInForce.GoodTillCanceled` = `GTC`; `OrderStatus.CanceledIoc` = `canceledIOC`).
- Candles and order book levels are positional JSON arrays on the wire; `BitvavoKline` and `BitvavoOrderBookEntry` hide that.
- Query strings and JSON bodies are sorted ordinally, case-insensitively. DELETE `/v2/order` and `/v2/orders` send parameters in the query; atomic cancel and the institutional DELETEs send a JSON body (signed).
- Signature: HMAC-SHA256 hex (lower case) over `timestamp + METHOD + "/v2/path[?query]" + body`.

## Pitfalls

1. `operatorId` is required on place, update, cancel, cancel all, atomic cancel (typed: `BitvavoPlaceOrderRequest.OperatorId`, `BitvavoUpdateOrderRequest.OperatorId`, `CancelOrderAsync(market, operatorId, ...)`, `CancelOrdersAsync(operatorId, market)`; Shared: exchange parameter `OperatorId`, `long`). Requests without it are rejected by Bitvavo. Reads need none.
2. `clientOrderId` must be a UUID and unique per market (code 220 `DuplicateClientOrderId`). `Guid.NewGuid().ToString()`; Shared: `GenerateClientOrderId()`.
3. `pricePrecision` is null on every live market: use `TickSize`. A price off the grid is code 422.
4. Fee rates are fractions: `0.0015` = 0.15 %. `BitvavoMarketFee.Maker` and `Taker`, `BitvavoFeeTier.Maker` and `Taker`, `BitvavoFill.Fee` (an amount in `FeeCurrency`). The Shared `SharedFee` is a percentage.
5. `Amount` (base asset) and `AmountQuote` (quote asset) are mutually exclusive (code 236); an update cannot switch between them (239); a market order cannot be updated (234). `AmountQuote` is meant for market orders and for stop-loss and take-profit without a limit price.
6. `AddBitvavo(o => o.ApiCredentials = ...)` gives credentials to REST only. Use `(BitvavoOptions o) => ...`.
7. Public endpoints stay unsigned, even with credentials, and use the per-IP budget; the report endpoints are public too. Signed endpoints use the per-account budget.
8. Weights that bite: `GetOpenOrdersAsync()` and `CancelOrdersAsync(operatorId)` without a market cost 100 (10 % of the 1000-point minute budget), `GetTicker24hAsync()` without a market 25, `WithdrawCryptoAsync` 25.
9. The account channel gives `order` and `fill` events only. No balances, no ticker, no book on the socket. A subscribe is "sent" = success; wrong markets are not reported; Bitvavo `error` events are not routed.
10. Order and fill events have no guaranteed order; reconcile with REST after reconnects.
11. Candle `startTime` and `endTime` must align with the interval; public and own trades windows are at most 24 h.
12. `GetOrderHistoryAsync` also returns open orders. `GetOpenOrdersAsync` without a market returns every market.
13. Cancel-on-disconnect: minimum 10 s, 0 removes the group, one group by default, not for market orders; the heartbeat is never counted by the limiter.
14. API withdrawals skip 2FA and e-mail confirmation. The address must be in the address book. `WithdrawCryptoAsync` needs `Network` (names from `BitvavoAsset.Networks`).
15. Status `Trading` only: filter markets by `BitvavoMarketStatus.Trading` before ordering.
16. `BitvavoAccountInfo.Capabilities` is not part of the v2.10.0 spec response: do not depend on it.
17. Code 109 (timeout) is not transient: the operation may have happened. Read the order back before retrying. HTTP 429 is not backed off automatically.
18. Order placement over WebSocket (`privateCreateOrder`) is not implemented. Place, update and cancel over REST.
19. `SharedClient` (V1) is kept for compatibility; new code uses `SharedApi` / `IBitvavoSharedApiClient`. Shared exchange parameters need the right value type (`1L`, `string[]`, `TriggerReference`).
20. `BitvavoExchange` and `BitvavoRateLimiters` live in the namespace `Bitvavo.Net.Objects.Internal` (public types).
21. No testnet and no dry-run or validate-only flag: every order call hits the live account. Test with the smallest amount the market allows (`MinOrderInQuoteAsset`).
22. `GetTicker24hAsync`, `GetTickerBookAsync`, `GetTickerPricesAsync` always return `IEnumerable<T>`: with a market filter the collection holds one item.

## Not implemented

- Public WebSocket `ticker`, `ticker24h` and `book` channels.
- `SymbolOrderBook`, trackers (`ITrackerFactory`), user-client-provider (multi-user).
- WebSocket request/response actions (`privateCreateOrder` etc.).
- WebSocket `error` event routing.
- Balance subscription (Bitvavo's account channel emits only order and fill events).
- Batch orders (no Bitvavo endpoint). Futures and margin (Bitvavo is spot only).
- Custom or sandbox environment (none exists); dry-run or validate-only order flag (none exists).
- Not measured without live credentials: whether the signed budget is per API key or per account (the limiter assumes per account), the reply to a rejected socket `authenticate`, the firing direction of stop loss and take profit (the usual meaning is assumed).

## Anti-hallucination checklist

Before finalizing generated code:

- Uses `BitvavoRestClient` / `BitvavoSocketClient` (or the injected interfaces), the right sub-client (`ExchangeData`, `Account`, `Trading`, `Funding`, `Report`, `Institutional`) and `SpotApi` (spot is the only API: no futures, no margin).
- Checks `.Success` before `.Data`, on every REST result and every subscription result.
- Orders carry `OperatorId`; `ClientOrderId` is a UUID; price is a multiple of `TickSize`; `Amount` xor `AmountQuote`.
- Funding calls use `SpotApi.Funding`, not `SpotApi.Account`.
- Credentials via `BitvavoCredentials`; both transports covered when DI is used.
- No WebSocket ticker, book or balance subscription; no `SymbolOrderBook`; no batch order call; no testnet environment.
- REST result type written as `HttpResult<T>`, subscription result as `WebSocketResult<UpdateSubscription>`.
- Shared API: capability looked up with `GetCapability<T>()` and null-checked, exchange parameters `OperatorId` (`long`) and `Markets` (`string[]`) supplied.
- No `.Result` or `.Wait()`; subscriptions unsubscribed at shutdown; clients reused and disposed.
- Weights considered for loops: market filters on open orders and tickers.
